title: ACT
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public ACT test specifications. Not a capture of past test questions.

items.stem: Which choice most effectively combines the two sentences to clarify that the volunteers worked despite the rain? The volunteers worked through the night. The rain fell steadily.
options: The volunteers worked through the night even though the rain fell steadily.
The volunteers worked through the night, the rain fell steadily.
The volunteers worked through the night; meanwhile rain.
The rain fell steadily the volunteers worked through the night.
items.explanation: Choice A uses the subordinating phrase 'even though' to show the contrast between the volunteers' work and the rain; the other choices create comma splices or sentence fragments.

items.stem: Which choice is punctuated correctly in its use of both the possessive apostrophe and the joining of two independent clauses?
options: The dogs collar was loose, it slipped off during the walk.
The dog's collar was loose; it slipped off during the walk.
The dog's collar was loose, it slipped off during the walk.
The dogs' collar was loose it slipped off during the walk.
items.explanation: The apostrophe marks the singular possessive 'dog's', and a semicolon correctly joins two independent clauses; the others misplace the apostrophe or use a comma splice.

items.stem: Which choice maintains a consistent verb tense throughout the sentence? Last summer she hiked the trail, camps beside a lake, and photographed eagles.
options: hiked the trail, camps beside a lake, and photographs eagles
hikes the trail, camped beside a lake, and photographs eagles
hiked the trail, camped beside a lake, and photographed eagles
hiked the trail, camping beside a lake, and photographs eagles
items.explanation: The sentence begins in the past tense with 'hiked', so 'camped' and 'photographed' keep the series consistently in the past; the other choices shift tense mid-series.

items.stem: Which choice is grammatically correct in its use of the comparative or superlative form? Of the two routes, the northern one is the ______ scenic.
items.explanation: When comparing exactly two items, the comparative 'more' is required; the superlative 'most' applies only to three or more items, and 'mostly' means mainly.

items.stem: Which choice correctly completes the sentence with the proper relative pronoun? The coach praised the players ______ scored the final goal.
items.explanation: The pronoun is the subject of 'scored', so the subjective form 'who' is correct; 'whom' is objective, 'which' refers to things, and 'whose' shows possession.

items.stem: Which choice corrects the dangling modifier in the sentence? Running down the street, the bus was caught by the boy.
options: Running down the street, the bus was caught by the boy.
Running down the street, the boy caught the bus.
The bus was caught, running down the street, by the boy.
The bus, running down the street, was caught by the boy.
items.explanation: The introductory phrase must modify the person doing the running, the boy; the other choices leave the bus, rather than the boy, as the one running.

items.stem: Which choice most precisely replaces the vague word 'good' to describe a highly effective legal argument? The lawyer made a good case for her client.
items.explanation: 'Compelling' precisely conveys that the argument was convincing and forceful, whereas the other choices describe mere pleasantness or bare adequacy.

items.stem: Which choice is a complete sentence rather than a fragment or a run-on?
options: Because the storm knocked out the power.
The storm knocked out the power, postponing the festival that the town.
Knocked out the power during the storm.
Because the storm knocked out the power, the town postponed the festival.
items.explanation: Only the first choice contains an independent clause with a subject and verb; the others are a dependent fragment, an incomplete construction, and a phrase.

items.stem: Which choice most concisely states the idea without changing the meaning? Due to the fact that it was raining, the game was canceled.
options: Because it was raining, the game was canceled.
Due to the fact that it was raining, the game was canceled.
Owing to the fact of rain, the game was called off and canceled.
The game was canceled due to the fact that there was rain.
items.explanation: 'Because' expresses the same cause as the wordy phrase 'due to the fact that' in fewer words; the other choices repeat the padding or add redundancy.

items.stem: Which choice correctly repairs the comma splice in the sentence? The museum closed early, the staff needed time to clean.
options: The museum closed early, the staff needed time to clean.
The museum closed early; the staff needed time to clean.
The museum closed early, but the staff needing time to clean.
The museum closed early the staff needed time to clean.
items.explanation: A semicolon correctly separates two independent clauses; the comma alone is a splice, the 'but' clause is incomplete, and the last choice has no separation at all.

items.stem: Which choice creates parallel structure in the series? The job requires patience, attention to detail, and ______.
items.explanation: The series is built from nouns ('patience', 'attention'), so the single noun 'reliability' keeps the list parallel; the other choices switch to verb phrases or a clause.

items.stem: Which transition word or phrase best connects the two ideas? The bridge was narrow. ______, only one car could cross at a time.
items.explanation: The second sentence states a result of the narrow bridge, so the cause-and-effect transition 'Consequently' fits; the others signal contrast or illustration.

items.stem: Which choice correctly completes the sentence so that the verb agrees with its subject? The collection of rare coins ______ displayed in the east hall.
items.explanation: The subject is the singular 'collection', not the plural 'coins', so the singular verb 'is' is required; the other choices are plural forms.

items.stem: Which choice uses the apostrophe correctly to show possession? The three ______ coats were hung by the door.
items.explanation: 'Children' is already an irregular plural, so possession is shown by adding apostrophe-s; the other forms add the possessive to a nonword or omit it.

items.stem: Which choice removes the redundancy from the sentence while preserving its meaning? The final outcome in the end was a surprise to everyone.
options: The final outcome in the end was a surprise to everyone.
The outcome in the end was a final surprise.
The final outcome was a surprise to everyone.
In the end, the final outcome was surprising in the end.
items.explanation: 'Final' already implies the end, so 'in the end' repeats the same idea; the other choices keep or multiply the redundancy.

items.stem: If 3x + 7 = 22, what is the value of x?
items.explanation: Subtract 7 from both sides to get 3x = 15, then divide by 3 to find x = 5; the other values do not satisfy the equation.

items.stem: What is the slope of the line that passes through the points (2, 3) and (6, 11)?
items.explanation: Slope equals the change in y over the change in x, so (11 - 3) / (6 - 2) = 8 / 4 = 2; the other choices invert or misread the differences.

items.stem: A jacket originally priced at 80 dollars is sold at a 25 percent discount. What is the sale price?
items.explanation: A 25 percent discount removes 20 dollars from 80, leaving 60 dollars; 20 dollars is only the discount amount, and the others misstate the reduction.

items.stem: What are the solutions to the equation x squared minus 5x plus 6 equals 0?
items.explanation: The expression factors as (x - 2)(x - 3), giving x = 2 and x = 3; the signed and factor-pair alternatives do not make the expression zero.

items.stem: If x plus y equals 10 and x minus y equals 4, what is the value of x?
items.explanation: Adding the two equations eliminates y and gives 2x = 14, so x = 7; the other values either equal y or do not satisfy both equations.

items.stem: The average of five numbers is 12. If four of the numbers are 8, 10, 14, and 16, what is the fifth number?
items.explanation: A mean of 12 over five numbers gives a total of 60; the four known numbers sum to 48, so the fifth number is 60 minus 48, or 12.

items.stem: A triangle has a base of 10 centimeters and a height of 6 centimeters. What is its area?
items.explanation: The area of a triangle is one half times base times height, so 0.5 times 10 times 6 equals 30; 60 is the product without the factor of one half.

items.stem: Which expression is equivalent to the product of x cubed and x to the fifth power?
options: 2 times x to the eighth power
items.explanation: When multiplying powers with the same base, add the exponents, so 3 plus 5 gives x to the eighth power; the other choices multiply exponents or add coefficients.

items.stem: A car travels at a constant speed of 60 miles per hour. How far does it travel in 2.5 hours?
items.explanation: Distance equals rate times time, so 60 times 2.5 equals 150 miles; the other values correspond to different times or a mistaken product.

items.stem: If f of x equals 2x squared minus 3, what is the value of f of 4?
items.explanation: Substitute 4 for x to get 2 times 16 minus 3, which equals 29; the other choices square incorrectly or forget the subtraction.

items.stem: A right triangle has legs of length 6 and 8. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
items.explanation: By the Pythagorean theorem, the hypotenuse squared is 36 plus 64, or 100, so the hypotenuse is 10; 14 is simply the sum of the legs.

items.stem: Which value of x satisfies the inequality 2x minus 3 is greater than 7?
items.explanation: Adding 3 and dividing by 2 gives x greater than 5, so only 6 satisfies the inequality; 5 yields equality and the smaller values fail it.

items.stem: A bag contains 3 red marbles and 7 blue marbles. If one marble is drawn at random, what is the probability that it is red?
items.explanation: There are 3 red marbles among 10 total, so the probability is 3/10; 3/7 compares red to blue rather than to the whole bag.

items.stem: What is the next term in the arithmetic sequence 4, 9, 14, 19, and so on?
items.explanation: Each term increases by 5, so adding 5 to 19 gives 24; the other values use a different common difference or skip a term.

items.stem: A circle has a radius of 5 inches. What is its circumference, in inches, in terms of pi?
items.explanation: Circumference equals 2 times pi times the radius, so 2 times 5 gives 10 pi; 25 pi is the area, not the circumference.

items.stem: A passage describes how a small town restored its riverfront by removing concrete and replanting native grasses. According to the passage, what was the main effect of the restoration?
options: Property values fell sharply along the river.
The town replaced the river with a parking lot.
Native wildlife returned and flooding decreased.
The river was diverted away from the town.
items.explanation: The passage links the restoration to a return of wildlife and reduced flooding; the other choices contradict the described outcome or invent details.

items.stem: A passage notes that a scientist's early experiments failed repeatedly, yet she kept detailed records that later guided her breakthrough. Which inference is best supported?
options: She abandoned science after her first failure.
Her records were destroyed before she succeeded.
She succeeded on her very first attempt.
Her careful record-keeping contributed to her eventual success.
items.explanation: The text ties her detailed records to the later breakthrough, supporting the inference that the records helped; the other choices conflict with the passage.

items.stem: In the sentence about lukewarm support from a committee, the word lukewarm most nearly means which of the following?
items.explanation: Used figuratively, 'lukewarm' describes support that is mild or lacking in enthusiasm; the literal temperature terms and 'reliable' miss that meaning.

items.stem: A passage states that honeybees communicate the location of food by performing a waggle dance. According to the passage, what does the dance convey?
options: The age of the queen bee
The direction and distance of a food source
items.explanation: The passage says the dance communicates a food source's location, meaning its direction and distance; the other choices are details the passage does not mention.

items.stem: An author recounts the history of a failed invention in order to do which of the following?
options: Prove that all inventors are careless
Advertise a new product for sale
Explain how the failure led to a useful later technology
items.explanation: A discussion of a failed invention typically aims to show how it paved the way for later progress; the other choices are unsupported or out of tone.

items.stem: A narrator describes a crumbling seaside hotel with obvious fondness while recalling childhood summers there. The narrator's tone is best described as which of the following?
items.explanation: Fond memories of childhood summers create a warm, wistful tone, or nostalgia; hostility, indifference, and fear do not match the described affection.

items.stem: A passage compares two migrating bird species and notes that one travels at night while the other travels by day. Which statement best captures the contrast?
options: The two species migrate at different times of day.
Both species migrate only at night.
The two species migrate to the same location at the same time.
items.explanation: The passage sets one night-migrating species against a day-migrating one, so the contrast is their different times of travel; the others erase that difference.

items.stem: According to a passage, a volcanic eruption blocked sunlight for months and global temperatures then dropped. Which cause-and-effect relationship does the passage describe?
options: Reduced sunlight led to cooler temperatures.
The eruption had no effect on temperature.
items.explanation: The passage presents blocked sunlight as the cause and falling temperatures as the effect; the other choices reverse or deny that relationship.

items.stem: In a passage arguing for urban gardens, one paragraph lists the costs of importing produce. That paragraph mainly serves to do which of the following?
options: Provide evidence supporting the author's argument
items.explanation: Listing import costs supplies reasons in favor of local gardens, so the paragraph supports the argument; the other choices misread its role in the passage.

items.stem: A passage describes a chef who first learns a recipe, then alters it, and finally invents a new dish. According to the passage, what does the chef do last?
items.explanation: The sequence places inventing the new dish after learning and altering, so that is the final action; the other choices name earlier steps or events not in the passage.

items.stem: A passage is written from the perspective of a traveler recalling a journey years later. Which phrase best indicates the narrator's point of view?
options: looking back on that long-ago summer
you will now board the train
the train departs at noon today
items.explanation: A phrase about looking back on a past summer signals a first-person recollection; the other phrases address the reader or describe immediate actions.

items.stem: In the sentence stating that her argument was sound and convinced the panel, the word sound most nearly means which of the following?
items.explanation: Here 'sound' describes an argument that is logical and well founded, meaning valid; the remaining choices use unrelated senses of the word.

items.stem: A passage reports that a plant grown in shade produced fewer flowers than the same species grown in full sun. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: Sunlight has no effect on flowering.
Sunlight may increase flower production in this species.
The shaded plant produced more flowers.
items.explanation: Since the sunlit plant flowered more, the data suggest sunlight may boost flowering; the other options overstate the finding or reverse it.

items.stem: An author claims that daily reading improves vocabulary. Which piece of evidence would best support that claim in the passage?
options: Reading is a popular hobby among adults.
Many books are sold each year.
Libraries are quiet places to study.
Students who read daily scored higher on a vocabulary test.
items.explanation: A test showing daily readers with higher vocabulary scores directly supports the claim; popularity, sales, and quietness do not address vocabulary growth.

items.stem: A passage explains that a new bridge reduced travel time but raised local taxes. Which statement best summarizes the passage?
options: The bridge brought a benefit along with a cost.
The bridge had only drawbacks for the town.
The taxes were lowered to fund the bridge.
Travel time increased after the bridge opened.
items.explanation: Shorter travel and higher taxes mean the bridge offered both a benefit and a cost; the other choices misstate or deny one of these effects.

items.stem: A table shows that as the temperature of a solution rose from 20 to 60 degrees Celsius, the time for a reaction fell from 40 to 10 seconds. What does the data indicate?
options: Higher temperature is associated with a slower reaction.
Higher temperature is associated with a faster reaction.
Temperature has no effect on reaction time.
items.explanation: Falling reaction time as temperature rises means the reaction sped up, so higher temperature accompanies a faster reaction; the other choices invert or ignore the trend.

items.stem: A student wants to test whether fertilizer affects plant height. Which setup would best isolate the effect of fertilizer?
options: Grow one plant with fertilizer and one without, giving them different amounts of water.
Grow every plant with fertilizer and measure height once.
Grow identical plants with and without fertilizer while holding water and light constant.
Change the amount of light for each plant.
items.explanation: Isolating one variable requires changing only fertilizer while keeping water and light the same; the other setups introduce extra variables or omit a comparison group.

items.stem: A graph of a predator and its prey shows the prey population rising and falling, with the predator population peaking shortly after each prey peak. What does this pattern suggest?
options: The prey population is unaffected by predators.
The predator population stays constant over time.
The predator population responds to changes in the prey population.
items.explanation: Predators peaking just after prey peaks suggests predator numbers track prey availability; the other choices contradict the cycles shown in the graph.

items.stem: In an experiment testing a new antibiotic, one group of bacteria receives the antibiotic and another receives no treatment. What is the purpose of the untreated group?
options: It serves as a control for comparison.
It guarantees the antibiotic will work.
It duplicates the treated group exactly.
items.explanation: An untreated group provides a baseline against which the antibiotic's effect is judged; the other options misstate the role of a control group.

items.stem: Three students measure the length of the same table and report 1.50 meters, 1.49 meters, and 1.51 meters. What do these results most likely indicate about their measurements?
options: The measurements are precise and close to one another.
The table changed length between measurements.
The students used no measuring tool.
items.explanation: Readings that differ by only about a centimeter show high precision; the other choices exaggerate the spread or invent explanations.

items.stem: A student observes that a white powder dissolves in water and the mixture fizzes and warms. Which observation most strongly suggests a chemical change?
options: The powder dissolves in the water.
The water was clear before mixing.
The mixture fizzes and releases gas.
The powder was white to begin with.
items.explanation: Fizzing and gas release signal a new substance forming, the hallmark of a chemical change; dissolving and the initial colors describe physical properties.

items.stem: A metal spoon left in a hot cup of soup becomes warm to the touch. Which process best explains this?
options: The spoon generates its own heat.
Cold moves from the spoon into the soup.
The soup loses no energy to the spoon.
Heat is conducted from the soup to the spoon.
items.explanation: Heat flows from the hotter soup to the cooler spoon by conduction; the spoon does not make heat, and cold does not move on its own.

items.stem: A chart shows that a population of fish declined steadily by about 10 percent each year for five years. If the trend continues, what is most likely to happen next year?
options: The population will stay exactly the same.
items.explanation: A steady annual decline implies the population will keep falling if the pattern holds; the other choices contradict the established downward trend.

items.stem: An experiment varies the amount of sunlight given to seedlings and measures their growth. Which is the independent variable?
items.explanation: The variable the experimenter deliberately changes is the independent variable, here the amount of sunlight; growth is the measured dependent variable.

items.stem: A diagram shows water flowing from a higher reservoir to a lower one through a pipe. What drives the water through the pipe?
options: The difference in height between the reservoirs
The shape of the reservoirs alone
items.explanation: Water flows downhill because of the height difference, which creates the pressure that moves it; pipe color, room temperature, and shape do not drive the flow.

items.stem: Birds on an island have beaks that vary in size, and after a drought only large seeds remain. Which explanation best fits the survival of large-beaked birds?
options: Large beaks make birds lighter so they can fly farther.
Small seeds are easier for large-beaked birds to eat.
Beak size has no relationship to diet.
Large beaks help birds eat the remaining large seeds.
items.explanation: If only large seeds remain, birds able to crack them with large beaks survive better; the other choices misstate the diet or deny any link between beak size and food.

items.stem: A table reports that a plant grew 2 centimeters in week one, 4 centimeters in week two, and 6 centimeters in week three. What is the average growth per week?
items.explanation: The sum of the weekly growth is 12 centimeters, and dividing by three weeks gives 4 centimeters per week; the other values misapply the average.

items.stem: A scientist predicts that plants watered with salt water will grow less than plants watered with fresh water. The results show both groups grow equally. What should the scientist conclude?
options: The data do not support the hypothesis.
Salt water always helps plants grow.
items.explanation: Since the two groups grew the same, the prediction of reduced salt-water growth is not supported; the other choices misread the result or invent a claim.

items.stem: A sample is a solid at room temperature, conducts electricity when melted, and forms ions in water. Which type of substance does this describe?
items.explanation: A solid that conducts when molten and forms ions in water fits an ionic compound; gases and metals do not match all of these properties.

items.stem: Two parent plants that are both heterozygous for flower color, written Pp, are crossed, where P is dominant for purple. What fraction of offspring is expected to show purple flowers?
items.explanation: A Pp by Pp cross yields one PP, two Pp, and one pp, so three of four offspring carry a dominant P and appear purple; one quarter would be white.
